a1-n-eintritt: At the museum desk you pay ten euros for permission to go inside, and children get a cheaper price.
A sign on the club door says: free for ladies before 11 p.m. What does the sign say is free?
The swimming pool asks you to pay at the cash desk before you may come in. What do you pay?
a1-n-name: At the doctor's reception the nurse asks what you are called, so she can look you up in the list.
On the form there are two boxes: first name and family ...
You meet a stranger at a party and say: Hello, I am Ali. What is the word for what you tell about yourself?
a1-pr-bisschen: A friend asks if you speak German. You say: only a small amount, not very much.
The waiter asks if you want sugar in the coffee, and you answer: just a tiny amount, please.
The doctor asks how much you smoke, and you say that you only smoke a very small amount. Which word means 'a little'?
a1-n-tee: On a cold evening you pour hot water over leaves in a cup and add a slice of lemon.
When you are sick, your grandmother brings you a hot herbal drink with honey, not coffee.
In England people like to drink a hot drink with milk at five o'clock in the afternoon. What is it?
a1-v-empfehlen: A friend says that the new Italian restaurant is great and that you should go there.
The waiter says that the fish is very good today and suggests that you try it.
A teacher says that the book is excellent and advises all the students to buy it.
a1-adj-tot: You find a bird on the street that no longer moves or breathes. It is no longer alive.
The old flowers in the vase have stopped living, so you throw them away.
The doctor says that the man in the accident no longer has a heartbeat. Which adjective describes him?
a1-n-glas: You pour milk into a clear container made of a transparent material, from which you drink.
On the table there is a small transparent container for jam with a metal lid.
The waiter brings the drinks and a clear vessel for each guest. What does he put on the table?
a1-adv-zurueck: After a week in Rome you come home again. Which adverb means 'to the place you came from'?
You lent your friend a pen yesterday. Now you ask him to give it to you again. Which adverb means 'to the original place'?
You borrow a book and promise to bring it to the library again next week. Which adverb means 'back'?
a1-n-saft: At breakfast the children drink a sweet orange drink, pressed from fruit, not milk.
The waiter asks what you want to drink and you choose an apple drink without alcohol.
At the party there is wine, beer and a drink made from squeezed fruit for the children.
a1-v-ausmachen: It is bedtime, so you press the button on the lamp and the room goes dark.
The TV is still running, but nobody watches. You press the button on the remote so that it is off.
Two friends agree on a time and place to meet next Tuesday. They arrange a date.
a1-n-bogen: The teacher gives each pupil one big single piece of paper for the test.
At the post office you ask for a printed page that holds a whole block of stamps.
In the sport shop you see a curved weapon with a string which is used to shoot arrows.
a1-n-schwester: At a family party a girl is dancing. She has the same parents as you.
You say: I have one brother and one female sibling. Who is she?
A little boy shows a picture of his mother, his father and the girl who grows up in his house, his female sibling.
a1-n-reisebuero: You walk into a shop to ask an employee about flight prices and hotels for your summer holiday.
You cannot find a cheap flight online, so you go to an office that plans trips and sells holidays.
A couple asks for catalogues for a trip to Spain at an agency. What kind of business is it?
a1-adj-wichtig: Your boss says that tomorrow's meeting is something that matters a lot, so you must not be late.
The teacher says to listen carefully because this part of the lesson is very significant.
A doctor says that it is of great value to drink enough water. Which adjective describes this?
a1-v-tun: A mother asks the child what he is doing in the garden. He says that he does nothing special.
The doctor says you can do something for your health, namely go for a walk every day.
A friend asks what you can do for him. Which common verb means 'to do'?
a1-n-doppelzimmer: You and your wife book a hotel room with one large bed for two people for the weekend.
At the hotel reception the clerk asks if you want a room for one person or for two.
Two friends travelling together ask for a room with two beds at the guest house. What kind of room?
a1-n-strasse: The taxi driver turns at the traffic light and drives along a long paved way with houses on both sides.
You look for an address and ask where the way with the house numbers is.
A child is told not to run across the paved way where the cars drive. What is it called?
a1-n-montag: After the weekend, you go back to work. It is the first working day of the week.
The day between Sunday and Tuesday. Many people dislike it.
The museum is closed on the first day of the week. Which day?
a1-v-bekommen: On your birthday you are happy to be handed a book by your friend.
You wait for the postman and finally the parcel arrives. You obtain it.
The doctor says that you will receive the results of your test on Friday.
a1-adv-lange: You waited at the bus stop for a very long period, nearly an hour. Which adverb describes this duration?
The film was boring and seemed to last for many hours. Which word describes how much time passed?
Your friend has lived in Berlin for many years. Which adverb means 'for a long time'?
a1-n-pass: At the border the officer opens your small booklet with your photo and country on the cover and stamps a page.
Before you travel abroad, you apply at the town hall for an official document that shows your identity and citizenship.
The airline employee asks you for the document that proves who you are, so that you can fly to another country.
a1-adj-geoeffnet: The sign on the bakery says that the shop is ready for customers until 6 p.m.
The window is wide apart. The fresh air comes into the room.
On Sunday the pharmacy is not shut. Which adjective describes it?
a1-n-dusche: In the morning you stand under warm water from above to wake up and wash.
In the hotel bathroom there is a small cabin with a glass door and a hot water tap above.
After sports you clean yourself in a cabin with a water head at the gym. What is it?
a1-pr-wir: You and your friends are going to the cinema tonight. You say that you and the others are going. Which word means 'I and others'?
You and your wife are tired. You say that you two are tired. Which pronoun covers yourself and another person?
A teacher includes herself and the whole class when she says: let us read the text. Which pronoun means 'I together with others'?
a1-v-anklicken: On the website you press the mouse button on the blue link to open the page.
The teacher says that you should use the mouse to press the button 'Start' on the screen.
To order, you press the 'Buy now' button on the shop's website with your mouse. Which verb?
a1-n-gruss: At the end of the letter you write 'best wishes' and sign your name. What is this friendly sentence called?
Your friend on holiday sends you a postcard with kind words. What noun describes the kind words?
A soldier raises his hand to his forehead when he meets an officer. What is this sign of respect?
a1-n-dienstag: The day after Monday, when the week has just begun but is not yet in the middle.
Your language class is on the second working day of the week at six o'clock.
A friend asks which day of the week is between Monday and Wednesday.
a1-n-halle: The handball team plays in a huge building with a high roof and a wooden floor.
At the airport you wait for your flight in a big room with shops and seats.
The market takes place in a big room with a high roof, in which many stalls sell vegetables and cheese.
a1-v-bedeuten: You see a strange road sign and ask your friend what it indicates.
You do not know a word in the text, so you look it up in the dictionary to find out its sense.
A red light on the dashboard of the car is on. You ask: what does it signal?
a1-n-zeit: You ask a stranger on the street what the clock says, because you are late.
Your boss says you should plan your work well, because you have only a short period before the deadline.
A friend says: I am very busy and have none of this to spare. What do you not have enough of?
a1-adj-grau: The sky is covered with clouds and it looks like it will rain. What colour is it?
Your grandfather's hair used to be black, but now it is the colour between black and white.
The elephant at the zoo has thick skin. What colour is it?
a1-adv-noch: You ask the waiter if there is still some cake left. Which adverb means 'still'?
The teacher says that the exam has not ended yet, and there are ten minutes left. Which adverb means 'yet' or 'still'?
You have finished your coffee and ask for one more, even bigger than before. Which adverb means 'even more'?
a1-n-auskunft: At the train station you go to a desk and ask where platform 5 is and when the next train leaves.
You call a service number to ask for the phone number of a company in another city.
At the hotel you ask the receptionist to give you details about local restaurants. Which noun?
a1-n-partnerin: At the wedding, the groom stands next to the woman with whom he will live his life.
A woman at the party says that the person she lives with is a doctor, and she is a woman.
In the business meeting, the lady from the other firm is a woman you work together with. Who is she?
a1-v-duschen: After a run you go into the bathroom and stand under the warm water to get clean.
Every morning you stand under the water from above before breakfast.
At the gym, after sports, the members clean themselves under the water in the cabin.
a1-n-durst: After a long walk in the hot sun you want to drink a lot of water. Which strong feeling?
The children come in from the garden and say that they would like a drink, because their throats are dry.
In the desert the tourists have no water left. What do they feel?
a1-n-verein: On Sundays you play football with your friends in a group that is registered in your town and has members who pay a fee.
Your uncle is the president of the group for chess players in your neighbourhood.
In Germany many people join an organisation for sports, music or hobbies. What do they join?
a1-v-bringen: You go to a party and carry a cake and a bottle of wine for the host.
The waiter walks to your table and carries the soup to you.
A taxi will take you to the airport tomorrow morning. Which verb describes carrying or taking someone or something to a place?
a1-n-europa: Germany, France and Italy are in this part of the world, between the Atlantic and Asia.
A tourist from America plans a two-week journey to visit London, Paris and Rome. Which continent?
On the map the continent with the Alps, the Rhine and the Danube is called what?
a1-adj-eilig: You see a man running to the bus in the rain. He has little time and must be somewhere fast.
A letter is marked 'must be done right now' by your boss. It cannot wait.
A mother says that she cannot talk now because she has to catch the train in five minutes. Which adjective describes her?
a1-n-getraenk: At the party you ask the host what you can have to drink, water, juice or beer. What is the general word?
On the restaurant menu there is a list of juices, wine, beer and water. What is that part of the menu called?
At the kiosk a sign says: cold things to drink for 1 euro. What is the word for water, cola and juice together?
a1-n-bank: You go to a place where you open an account and take out money.
In the park you sit on a long wooden seat under a tree and feed the birds.
The cashier tells you to deposit money at the place that keeps it safe for you.
a1-adv-oben: The bedroom is on the top floor of the house, not on the ground floor. Where is it?
You tell the child to look at the sky: the birds are flying in the high area. Which adverb?
The book is on the highest shelf, in the upper position. Which adverb describes the place?
a1-pr-sie-2: You look at your friend Anna and say that she is nice. Which word do you use for a female person?
You see two children playing and say that these children are happy. Which pronoun means 'they'?
You ask about a woman's bag and say it is very nice. Which word replaces a feminine noun like 'the bag'?
a1-v-suchen: You cannot find your keys, so you go through every room and every drawer to find them.
You search for a flat in the city and read many advertisements every day.
The tourist says that he is looking for the station. Which verb?
a1-n-bruder: At the football match a boy cheers next to you, who has the same parents as you.
You say: I have one sister and one male sibling. Who is he?
A girl says that her male sibling is two years older than she is.
a1-n-blume: For Mother's Day you buy a red rose with a long stem and put it in a vase.
In spring the garden is full of colourful tulips and daffodils.
The florist wraps a bunch of tulips in paper. What is she selling?
a1-n-papiere: At the checkpoint the officer says: please show your documents that prove who you are.
You lost your wallet with your cards and the documents that show your identity. What did you lose?
On arrival at the border you must hand over your passport and other official documents. What are these called?
a1-adj-hoch: The Alps have a mountain peak that reaches far into the sky. It is a very elevated mountain.
The church tower in the city is much taller than the houses around it.
The price in the shop is far above the normal level. Which adjective describes the level?
a1-v-rad-fahren: On Saturday you go from home to the lake on two wheels and with pedals, in the sun.
To keep fit, you do not use the car, but sit on a saddle and pedal to work every day.
A mother tells the child that he should wear a helmet when he does this on the road with his bike.
a1-n-lehrerin: At school a woman stands in front of the class and explains English to the pupils.
A woman in the language course corrects your homework and gives you marks.
Your daughter says that the woman who teaches her maths is very kind. Who is she?
a1-n-doktor: You have a very high temperature, so you visit a man in a white coat who examines you.
At the clinic, a person who has studied medicine for many years looks at your throat.
A letter begins with the title Dr. for the person who has completed a PhD. What title is used?
a1-v-gehen: It is a sunny day, so you do not take the bus. You move on foot to the park.
The party is boring, so you tell your friend that you want to leave now.
A child asks how he can reach the school. You say: you just walk along the street. Which verb?
a1-n-garten: Behind the house there is a piece of land with grass, flowers and apple trees where children play.
In spring your grandfather plants vegetables outside the house.
On summer evenings the family sits outside on a lawn behind the house and has a barbecue.
a1-adv-rechts: The driver says that the pharmacy is on the side of your right hand, after the traffic light.
You ask for the way. The woman says: go straight, and then on the side opposite to the left.
At the crossing the driver is told to turn in the direction opposite to left. Which adverb?
a1-n-bild: You hang a painting of a landscape above the sofa in the living room.
On the computer screen you open a photo that shows your family.
The teacher shows the class a drawing of a house and asks them to describe what they can see.
a1-adj-zufrieden: You get your exam result and see that it is just what you wanted. You feel content.
The customer says that the service in the hotel was all that he needed. He is pleased.
Your boss says that he has no complaints about your work. Which adjective describes his feelings?
a1-n-nacht: After the sun goes down, the sky is dark and people go to sleep.
The shop is open all day and all of the dark hours too. It never closes.
You wake up when it is still dark outside, at three o'clock. Which part of the day is it?
a1-v-fehlen: The teacher counts the pupils and sees that two pupils are not in the room today.
You cook a soup, but you notice that there is no salt in the house. Which verb describes that something is not there?
The child cries because he does not have his mother near him. He misses her.
a1-n-konto: At the bank you open a place where your salary is paid and from which your rent is taken.
You check your phone and see that you have 500 euros in your balance at the bank.
On the form you write your IBAN number, which belongs to this arrangement at the bank.
a1-n-flugzeug: You travel from Berlin to London in two hours, high in the sky, with wings and engines.
Children stand at the fence of the airport and look at the big machine that rises into the air.
At the airport you walk across the field to the machine with two wings, which will take you to Paris.
a1-pr-beide: Anna and Tom are very tired. You say that the two of them need a break. Which word covers the two?
The teacher says that the pupils, the girl and the boy, did the homework. Which word means 'the two of them'?
A mother has two sons. She says that she loves each and every one of the two. Which word means 'both'?
a1-n-empfaenger: On the parcel the post office writes the name and address of the person who will get the package.
In the email form there is a field at the top where you write the address of the person who will get your message.
The bank asks for the name of the person to whom you are sending the money. Which word?
a1-v-vermieten: You have an empty room in your flat, so you offer it to a student for 300 euros a month.
Your friend owns a house at the beach and allows tourists to stay there in summer for a fee.
You own a flat and make a contract with a tenant who will pay you every month. What do you, the owner, do?
a1-n-drittel: A cake is cut into three equal pieces. You eat one of them. What is the name for this fraction?
The teacher says: 1/3 of the pupils are absent today.
You pay one part of the three equal parts of the rent. Which noun?
a1-adj-kulturell: The city offers theatres, museums and concerts. Tourists like its events about art and history.
The festival is about the traditions and music of different countries. Which adjective describes it?
The foreign students have different habits and customs from their host country. Which adjective describes these differences?
a1-n-kino: On Friday night you buy popcorn and sit in a dark room to watch a big film on a huge screen.
The friends go to a building with several halls, where films are shown, in the city centre.
The family says that they will go to see the new film at a place with a big screen and many seats.
a1-adv-zurzeit: Your friend asks if you work. You say that you work in a hotel at this time, but later you will change.
The doctor says that he has no free appointment at present. Which adverb means 'currently'?
The teacher says that the library is closed for the time being, because of repairs. Which adverb?
a1-n-feierabend: It is 5 p.m., you close your laptop, say goodbye to your colleagues and go home from work.
The shop closes at six o'clock. After that the shop assistants stop work.
The man says to his wife: after work I will go to the gym, and in the evening we will eat together.
a1-v-wollen: A child says to his father that he desires an ice cream now.
The waiter asks what you would like to drink. You say that you desire a coffee. Which verb expresses a wish?
Your friend says that he has the plan to study medicine. Which modal verb expresses this wish?
a1-n-kind: A small person of five years old plays with his toys in the sandbox in the park.
At the doctor, the nurse asks the mother how old her son or daughter is. Which noun means a young person of either gender?
A family has two sons and a daughter. What do you call the young ones of the parents?
a1-n-brot: At the bakery you buy a big loaf with a brown crust to eat with butter and cheese.
For dinner the Germans often eat slices of this with sausage and cheese, instead of a hot meal.
The baker takes it from the oven in the morning. It is made from flour, water and yeast.
a1-v-schmecken: You try the soup that your mother cooks and say that the flavour in your mouth is great.
A friend asks you how the pizza is. You say: it has a delicious flavour.
The child says that the medicine has a horrible flavour. Which verb means to have a flavour?
a1-n-fehler: The teacher marks your test with a red pen where you wrote the wrong word.
In the email there is a wrong spelling. You see that something went wrong.
The computer program does not run, because there is a bug in it.
a1-adj-spaet: It is midnight. A friend phones and you say that it is far into the evening already.
The bus came at eleven instead of ten. It did not arrive on time.
Your boss is angry because you come to work after the normal start. Which adjective?
a1-n-vorwahl: You call a friend in Munich from Berlin. You need to dial some numbers before the phone number, such as 089.
On the business card the number begins with a short number for the city, then the personal number.
For international calls you add +49 for Germany. What do you call this first part of a phone number?
a1-n-dorf: The grandmother lives in a small place in the countryside with a church, a shop and about 300 people.
In the countryside there are fields, cows and only a few houses. It is much smaller than a town.
After the city you move to a small place where everyone knows everyone.
a1-v-unterschreiben: At the bank you write your name with a pen at the bottom of the contract to make it official.
The postman asks you to write your name on his phone to confirm that you received the parcel.
The teacher gives you a letter for your parents and asks them to put their name on the bottom line.
a1-adv-nie: You are asked if you have been in Asia. You say not once in your whole life.
The old man says that he does not smoke at any time, not even once.
A friend asks if you often come late. You say: not on any occasion. Which adverb means 'never'?
a1-n-deutschland: Berlin is the capital of this country in Central Europe, where you are learning the language.
On the map the country with Munich, Hamburg and Frankfurt is next to France and Poland.
A tourist from India asks: where do you live? You say in the country with the Rhine and the Alps, whose language you study. Which country?
a1-n-reise: Next month you will go for two weeks to Spain by plane, with hotel and beaches.
The train takes you across the whole country, and you need ten hours for this long trip.
A friend asks how your holiday was. You tell him about the places you saw on your way.
a1-pr-uns: Your friends say that they want to visit you and your wife next week. Which word means 'you and me' as the object?
You and your brother help yourselves to the food at the buffet. Which word means 'ourselves'?
You say to your friend that you two should help each other. Which word means 'each other'?
a1-n-mitte: On the map the city centre is in the middle of the town, with the market and the town hall.
You sit in the cinema in the row at the halfway point, neither at the front nor at the back.
A friend asks where the best place is to meet in the town. You say: right at the heart.
a1-v-anfangen: The teacher says: open your books, because the lesson is about to begin now.
At nine o'clock the film starts. It is the first minute.
Your friend says: I will take up a new job on Monday. Which verb describes the first moment of an activity?
a1-adj-schlecht: The milk in the fridge smells strange and is no longer good to drink.
You get a low mark in the test because you did not study. The result is poor.
The weather is terrible. It rains and is cold. Which adjective is the opposite of 'good'?
a1-n-verkaeuferin: In the shoe shop a woman helps you to find your size and takes the money at the cash desk.
At the bakery, a woman behind the counter gives you the bread and says: that is 3 euros.
The customer asks the woman who works in the shop if the dress is also available in blue.
a1-n-problem: Your car does not start and you must be at work in ten minutes. You have a difficulty.
The teacher asks the class to solve a difficult task in maths.
A friend says: I need help, I have some trouble with my computer. Which noun means a difficulty?
a1-v-fahren: You go to work by car, sitting behind the wheel on the road.
The train takes you from Berlin to Munich. You travel by train.
A child learns to ride on two wheels without his parents' help. Which verb describes going by a vehicle?
a1-n-arm: The doctor looks at the part of your body between the shoulder and the hand, because it hurts after a fall.
When you lift a heavy bag, you use the muscles in the part of the body next to the chest.
The baby is carried in the mother's limbs, between the shoulder and the hand.
a1-adv-hoch: The balloon flies upwards into the sky. Which adverb describes the direction?
The teacher says to the pupils: lift your hands into the air. Which adverb means 'up'?
The children throw the ball to a great height. Which adverb describes that?
a1-n-kunde: In the shop a man looks at shirts and wants to buy something. He is the person who pays for goods.
At the hairdresser's the woman says that the man in the chair is the person who uses her services.
The bank manager greets a man who has had an account with the bank for twenty years. Who is the man to the bank?
a1-adj-puenktlich: The train arrives exactly at 10:00, as planned, without any delay.
Your boss likes that you are always at your desk at 9:00, not one minute later.
The teacher thanks the pupils for coming exactly at the time of the lesson. Which adjective describes them?
a1-n-halbpension: At the hotel the price includes the room, breakfast and dinner, but not lunch.
The hotel offers a room with two meals a day, in the morning and in the evening. What is it called?
On the booking form you choose between only a room, a room with breakfast, or a room with breakfast and dinner.
a1-v-dauern: The flight from Berlin to London needs two hours. What does the flight do with respect to time?
You ask the doctor how much time the treatment will need. He says: about an hour.
The film runs for three hours. Which verb describes the length of time that something needs?
a1-n-lied: At the party everyone sings a happy tune for your birthday.
On the radio there is a piece of music with words, sung by a famous singer.
The child learns a short piece of music with words in the kindergarten.
a1-n-meer: On holiday you swim in salt water that goes as far as the horizon, with big waves.
Ships cross the huge body of water between continents.
In summer many tourists go to the coast to lie on the sand and look at the waves.
a1-n-aufgabe: The teacher gives you three exercises to do at home for tomorrow.
Your boss says that your duty this week is to organise the meeting.
In the exam there are ten questions to answer. Each one is a piece of work that you have to complete.
a1-v-erklaeren: You do not understand the grammar, so the teacher says it again, step by step, until you see how it works.
A tourist asks how the ticket machine works, so you show him how to use it.
The president says officially that the country has agreed to the new rules.
a1-n-balkon: On summer evenings you sit outside on a small platform attached to the wall of your flat, above the street, and drink tea.
In the flat on the third floor there are plants on a small platform outside the living room window.
A man stands on the small open platform on the first floor and waves to the people below.
a1-adj-rot: Tomatoes, strawberries and the stop signal of the traffic light all have this colour.
When you are embarrassed, your face becomes the colour of a ripe tomato.
The fire engine is painted with this bright colour and has a loud siren.
